newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end steady after early weakness.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end steady after early weakness.

text.p: Swiss shares recovered from early weakness to end little changed in quiet trade after Monday's 2.6 percent jump.
Dealers said insecurity about the development of U.S. stock markets kept a lid on shares, but directionless, yet volatile, trade may last until Friday, when new U.S. data are due.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) edged down 5.4 points to 4,582.6 points. The SMI may move beween 4,440 and 4,670 points in the next few sessions.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was off 4.16 points to 2,898.99 points.
A firmer U.S. dollar boosted industrials while financials were generally slightly lower.
Clariant, which released better-than-expected 1996 results last Friday, continued to soar. The stock rose 10 francs to 752.
Swissair also added to recent gains, climbing 45 francs to 1,330. The company on Friday released a 1996 net loss of nearly 500 million francs.
Roche and Novartis gave up ground, while Nestle, Ares-Serono, Sulzer, Buehrle, Holderbank and Rieter ended up.
Rieter said after bourse close 1996 net profit rose to 66.3 million francs from 57.3 million francs year-on-year.
UBS bearer shares were among the day's losers with a fall of 1.5 percent. CS Group and insurer Zurich ended higher.
